This looks considerably more feasible now than it would have been in 2015. There are historical archives, regional census projects, annual reports, and even some regional burns that publish their own annual attendance figures.

And your memory is largely correct. The first Texas burn was a little later, but the early geographical spread is particularly interesting.

## **1. The first sparks**

I've established these initial milestones:

|Year|Event|Location|Participants|
|---|---|---|---|
|1986|Burning Man|Baker Beach, San Francisco|~35|
|1987|Burning Man|Baker Beach, San Francisco|80|
|1988|Burning Man|Baker Beach, San Francisco|200|
|1989|Burning Man|Baker Beach, San Francisco|300|
|1990|Burning Man (unburned effigy)|Baker Beach, San Francisco|500|
|1990|Burning Man|Black Rock Desert, Nevada|~120|
|1997|Regional Network established|Texas, California, Canada|N/A|
|1998|Burning Man Texas|Austin, Texas|~30|
|1999|Burning Flipside|Texas||
|2004|Kiwiburn|New Zealand||
|2004|Nowhere|Aragón, Spain|~35|

Sources: Burning Man's [official history](https://history.burningman.org/timeline/?utm_source=chatgpt.com), [Regional Network history](https://burningman.org/global-events-groups/burning-man-regional-network/history-of-the-regional-network/?utm_source=chatgpt.com), Burning Flipside's own [historical reports](https://www.burningflipside.com/announcements/burning-flipside-2018-return-of-the-shadows-20-years-of-light-and-dark-public-information-report?utm_source=chatgpt.com), and an [interview with Nowhere co-founder Dave Bradshaw](https://www.histoiresordinaires.fr/Dave-Bradshaw-co-founder-of-an-alternative-festival_a760.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com).

Burning Man Project+3

Two particularly useful historical details:

- **Burning Flipside** originated as Burning Man Texas in 1998, adopting its current name in 1999.
    
- **Kiwiburn** is identified by Burning Man's official history as the first regional burn outside North America. Both Kiwiburn and Nowhere started in 2004.
    

The movement was already 18 years old when those first officially documented sparks appeared overseas.

## **2. I found an existing global dataset!**

This might save a substantial amount of work.

[**Burns Around the World (updated)**](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/19LLXY1Om77p6UG4Y9wEVw3uaYXSn23xj1yW3s3j8O5g/edit?gid=1618287697&utm_source=chatgpt.com)

A community-maintained Google spreadsheet with approximately 178 entries. Its columns include:

- Event name and first burn year
    
- Country, region and nearest town
    
- Map location
    
- Approximate ticket capacity and tickets sold
    
- Official recognition status
    
- Links to websites and AfterBurn reports
    

It isn't a historical attendance dataset, but it is an excellent starting catalogue. Some older fields are explicitly marked as unverified.

Google Sheets

## **3. Black Rock City: almost complete historical population data**

![Chart](data:image/png;base64,)

Burning Man attendance, 1986–2025. Zero in 2020–2021 represents cancellation of the official physical event, not the absence of unofficial gatherings.

The [official historical timeline](https://history.burningman.org/timeline/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) and a [compiled annual attendance table](https://camperchamp.com/usa/burning-man-statistics/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) provide essentially the entire series. Early estimates sometimes disagree, particularly for 1990.

camperchamp.com+1

We even have the temporary relocation to Fly Ranch / Hualapai Flat in 1997, before the event returned to Black Rock Desert in 1998.

This part of the animation can already be built.

Wikipedia+8

An interesting discovery: Playa del Fuego's precursor started only two months after the original Texas burn. So in 1998 we already have sparks on both sides of the continental US.

And if we include urban burner gatherings, the first European spark might actually be in London in 2001.

There is also a whole second generation of events to investigate: Kiez Burn, Burning Nest, MicroBurn, Fuego Austral, Where the Sheep Sleep, Waking Life, French and Swiss burns, Japan's regional burns, and the Eastern European ones. Some are explicitly burns, others are inspired by burner culture.

## **7. How I would structure the data collection project**

Given what we've found, I would avoid manually compiling one giant spreadsheet. This is now a good fit for a small agentic data archaeology project.

Two main tables:

`events.csv`

```
event_id,name,country,first_year,parent_event_id
burning_man,Burning Man,US,1986,
flipside,Burning Flipside,US,1998,burning_man
nowhere,Nowhere,ES,2004,burning_man
kiwiburn,Kiwiburn,NZ,2004,burning_man
afrikaburn,AfrikaBurn,ZA,2007,burning_man
```

`editions.csv`

```
event_id,year,location,lat,lon,population,metric,confidence,status,source_url
nowhere,2004,Bardenas Reales,,,35,attendance,high,held,...
nowhere,2005,Robres,,,68,attendance,high,held,...
nowhere,2020,Monegros,,,0,attendance,high,cancelled,...
```

The coordinates belong to individual editions, not events, because events move.

I'd also preserve the original source observations separately, so we don't lose conflicting figures when reconciling them.

### **Research pipeline**

|Phase|Approach|
|---|---|
|1. Discovery|Import both community spreadsheets and Burning Wiki|
|2. Historical discovery|Search archived regional calendars and newsletters year by year|
|3. Enrichment|One research agent per event, extracting all historical editions|
|4. Archaeology|Wayback Machine CDX API, Wikipedia revision history, abandoned websites|
|5. Geocoding|Resolve historical locations into coordinates|
|6. Reconciliation|Resolve conflicting attendance figures, aliases and duplicate events|
|7. Crowdsourcing|Ask local burner communities to fill remaining gaps|

An important distinction for the population data:

- Actual gate attendance
    
- Tickets sold
    
- Maximum ticket capacity
    
- Organizer estimate
    
- Media estimate
    
- Interpolated estimate
    

For your purposes, all six are useful. They just shouldn't be indistinguishable in the underlying dataset.

## **8. The visualization itself**

I know this isn't what you're asking to build yet, but I'd use a visual grammar something like this:

Illustrative population-to-glow mapping

Dark world map, warm glowing embers. New events briefly flare when founded, then settle into growing points of light.

- Size represents attendance, with a compressed scale so that smaller burns remain visible.
    
- Brightness pulses during the actual event dates, where known.
    
- Missing attendance data is represented by a small, dim spark rather than zero.
    
- Cancelled events go dark.
    
- Relocated events move.
    
- Documented parent-child relationships produce travelling sparks between locations.
    
- The year, number of active burns, countries and total attendance appear in a corner.
    

I would use MapLibre and deck.gl for the interactive version, with a deterministic rendering pipeline for exporting a video.

## **9. Where we are after this first search**

We have:

- Almost 40 years of Burning Man population figures.
    
- Five substantial regional historical attendance series.
    
- A catalogue of approximately 178 candidate events.
    
- Historical venue information for several early burns.
    
- A dozen or more promising archives.
    
- Global aggregate figures for recent years.
    

What remains incomplete is the systematic event-by-event extraction, especially for smaller European, Canadian, Asian and South American burns, discontinued events, and the years after 2019. I also haven't confidently identified the event you remember as Wikiburn.

I've deliberately not filled gaps with invented attendance estimates or assumed that an event happened every year after its foundation. And I haven't yet extracted the full global spreadsheet into a normalized dataset.

**I think the original project is very much worth resurrecting.** The most difficult part in 2015 was probably finding hundreds of scattered historical facts. That is precisely the sort of tedious, parallelizable research that modern LLM agents are particularly well suited to helping with.
